source_text:
Φανερὰ ἔσται ἡ Γαλιλαία καὶ ὁ Κάρμηλος. Νῦν ἀναστή σομαι, λέγει κύριος, νῦν
δοξασθήσομαι, νῦν ὑψωθήσομαι. Νῦν ὄψεσθε, νῦν αἰσχυνθήσεσθε.» Πρὸς γὰρ τοὺς
Ἰουδαίους τὸν λόγον ἀπετείνετο· νῦν ἀναστήσομαι ὅταν ἐγείρω τὸν Ἀδὰμ ὃν ἡ
παράβασις ἔρριψεν, νῦν δοξασθήσομαι ὅταν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν τῶν παθῶν συστήσω τὴν
ἀπάθειαν, νῦν ὑψω θήσομαι τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀπαρχὴν εἰς οὐρανοὺς ὑψῶν καὶ εἰς τὴν
καθέδραν τῶν χερουβὶν ἐπαίρων «τὴν τοῦ δούλου μορ φὴν» ἥνπερ ἐξ ὑμῶν
κέκτημαι, νῦν ὄψεσθε παυομέ νους τοὺς τύπους, ἀνθοῦσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν, νῦν
αἰσχυνθή σεσθε συκοφαντοῦντες ῥήμασιν καὶ ἡττώμενοι πράγμασιν, ὅτι τῷ θεῷ ἡ
δόξα, τῷ Πατρὶ καὶ τῷ Υἱῷ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύ ματι, νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας
τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.

1
orientation: Hesychius completes the Isaiah quotation and then expounds each now clause as the Lord speaking about raising Adam and exalting humanity.
pass_a_gloss: Galilee will be manifest and Carmel will be manifest. Now I will rise, says the Lord, now I will be glorified, now I will be exalted. Now you will see, now you will be put to shame. For he addressed the word to the Jews: now I will rise when I raise Adam whom the transgression cast down, now I will be glorified when I establish impassibility for the nations out of the sufferings, now I will be exalted while lifting your first fruit up into the heavens and while raising to the seat of the cherubim the form of a servant which I have acquired from you, now you will see the types ceasing and the truth blooming, now you will be put to shame while slandering with words and while being defeated by deeds, because to God be the glory, to the Father and to the Son and to the holy Spirit, now and always and into the ages of the ages. Amen.

lemmas.gloss: you will be put to shame

choices.why: brief glossary requires sufferings for Christ truly suffering in the flesh
brief glossary requires impassibility as freedom from suffering given through the risen Christ
brief glossary requires this exact phrase for the assumed humanity now exalted
brief glossary requires types for Old Testament shadows ceasing before fulfillment
brief glossary requires truth as the reality fulfilled in Christ contrasted with types

bible_refs.note: Φανερὰ ἔσται ἡ Γαλιλαία καὶ ὁ Κάρμηλος. Νῦν ἀναστήσομαι, λέγει κύριος, νῦν δοξασθήσομαι, νῦν ὑψωθήσομαι. Νῦν ὄψεσθε, νῦν αἰσχυνθήσεσθε

pass_b_english: "Galilee shall be seen, and Carmel shall be revealed. Now I will rise, says the Lord; now I will be glorified; now I will be exalted. Now you shall see; now you shall be put to shame (Isaiah 33:9-11)."

For Isaiah directed this word to the Jews. "Now I will rise" means, when I raise Adam, whom transgression cast down. "Now I will be glorified" means, when I establish for the nations impassibility from sufferings. "Now I will be exalted" means, as I lift your firstfruits to heaven and raise to the seat of the cherubim the form of a servant which I have taken from you.

"Now you shall see" means, as you watch the types come to an end and the truth bloom. "Now you shall be put to shame" means, as you slander with words and are defeated by deeds. To God be the glory, to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
notes: Source has spaced letter groups from printing: ὑψω θήσομαι, μορ φὴν, παυομέ νους, αἰσχυνθή σεσθε, Πνεύ ματι; reading is certain, glossed as continuous words; no text invented.

problems.quote: Hesychius says Isaiah directed this word to the Jews.
problems.source_quote:
Πρὸς γὰρ τοὺς
Ἰουδαίους τὸν λόγον ἀπετείνετο·
problems.why: Hesychius is the homilist speaking directly, not a third party; adding "Hesychius says" invents an external narrator absent from the Greek.
problems.fix: For Isaiah directed this word to the Jews.
problems.ruling: Greek has no Ἡσύχιος; Πρὸς γὰρ τοὺς Ἰουδαίους continues the homily, not third-party narration.

problems.quote: Now you shall see; now you shall be put to shame (Isaiah 33:9-10)."
problems.why: "Now you shall see; now you shall be put to shame" is from LXX Isaiah 33:11, so the reference omits verse 11.
problems.fix: Now you shall see; now you shall be put to shame (Isaiah 33:9-11)."
problems.ruling: Νῦν ὄψεσθε, νῦν αἰσχυνθήσεσθε tied to Isaiah 33:9–10 omits verse 11 for those clauses.
